body:
CLAIM: SNF therapy services (PT/OT/ST) are a covered type of service furnished by the SNF

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy must be specific and effective treatment for the condition; referral reasons fit treatment of functional decline

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be considered under accepted standards of medical practice to be specific and effective treatment"

CLAIM: A qualifying hospital stay appears documented, but SNF admission timing and level of care are not settled

CASE FACT QUOTED: "each contending that the beneficiary had a qualifying three-day stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Inpatient coverage depends on documented need for inpatient admission, not on length of stay alone; record facts do not settle this

CASE FACT QUOTED: "expected discharge within 24 hours"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: Admission to SNF after a qualifying hospital stay supports the basic post-hospital eligibility and coverage presumption

CASE FACT QUOTED: "was admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "there is a presumption that he or she meets the Medicare"

CLAIM: Home health at an assisted living facility can be covered if the facility is not primarily engaged in providing institutional care; facility type and homebound status are not stated

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "then Medicare will cover reasonable and necessary home health care furnished to these individuals"

CLAIM: Hospice/terminal-condition SNF care is not billed through Medicare Part A; only care unrelated to the terminal condition may be covered

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant does not contend that the SNF care at issue was unrelated to the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.3.1): "These bills are not processed by the A/B MAC (A) or (HHH)."

CLAIM: Therapy ended before the disputed dates of service

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She was discharged from OT on January 19, 2009, and from PT on January 22, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Frequent venipuncture/monitoring for diabetics is covered only within home health eligibility; homebound status and plan of care are not shown

CASE FACT QUOTED: "evidencing fluctuating blood sugar levels"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.13): "A stable insulin or noninsulin dependent diabetic would require monitoring every 2-3 months."

CLAIM: Hospital stay of more than 3 inpatient days counted by admission day, not discharge day

CASE FACT QUOTED: "hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day"

CLAIM: SNF admission on the day of hospital discharge meets the 30-day transfer requirement

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Admitted to SNF the day of discharge from a multi-day inpatient stay, meeting post-hospital requirements

CASE FACT QUOTED: "was first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Therapy furnished by the SNF is a covered service type

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Following readmission, the beneficiary received physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and nursing services."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy coverage turns on need for skilled care, not improvement potential; qualifying hospital stay and SNF admission facts are not clearly stated

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant asserts that the beneficiary made steady progress throughout physical therapy"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "Coverage for such skilled therapy services does not turn on the presence or absence of a beneficiary"

CLAIM: Therapist teaching of a maintenance program is covered if therapist skills are required; homebound status is not shown

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "instruction of the beneficiary or appropriate caregiver by a qualified therapist regarding a maintenance program is covered if the specialized skills, knowledge, and judgment"

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care is not skilled nursing

CASE FACT QUOTED: "His bowel and bladder functions are maintained by colostomy and urostomy."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "changing the colostomy bag does not become a skilled nursing service when the nurse provides it"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing visits to evaluate infection symptoms can be reasonable and necessary; homebound and plan-of-care status are not documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He had a recurrence of urinary tract infection around mid-point during the six-month period at issue."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The skilled nursing visit to change the catheter and to evaluate the patient would be reasonable and necessary"

CLAIM: Part-time or intermittent aide/nursing care is covered up to stated hour limits; patient eligibility is not established in the facts

CASE FACT QUOTED: "coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Services in a noncertified bed may be paid only under certain conditions

CASE FACT QUOTED: "did not have a certified bed available"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "the services may be paid under certain conditions, based on the limitation of liability provisions"

CLAIM: Admission followed a qualifying hospital stay

CASE FACT QUOTED: "both following a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: IRF care is covered only if all 42 CFR 412.622 requirements are met; the case facts do not show them

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing observation and assessment is a covered SNF service type

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.3): "Nursing services are considered skilled when they are so inherently complex that they can be safely and effectively performed only by"

CLAIM: Psychiatric-related skilled observation can be covered if carefully documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "There she was diagnosed with dementia, a behavioral disturbance, and psychosis not otherwise specified."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Skilled observation and assessment may also be required for patients whose primary condition and needs are psychiatric in nature"

CLAIM: IRF care is covered only if the 412.622 requirements are met; the facts do not settle all of them

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Two days later, on July 17, 2003, the beneficiary was transferred and admitted to the appellant"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: Documented functional decline with PT referral fits restoring lost function through skilled therapy.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E.’s functional status had declined as follows: her sitting balance was poor"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "requires a brief period of daily skilled physical therapy to restore lost functions, those services are reasonable and necessary"

CLAIM: PT assessment of strength and ADLs is a skilled need.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "The skills of a physical therapist are required for the ongoing assessment of a patient’s rehabilitation needs and potential."

CLAIM: Referral after hospitalization shows a decline needing evaluation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "E.M. was referred to OT due to an overall decline in transfers, range of motion, strength, and independence with ADLs."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "the amount, frequency, and duration of the services must be reasonable"

CLAIM: Passages address presumption of coverage, not clinical criteria; coverage rests on medical evidence in the file, which is not settled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "coverage would be determined based on a review of the medical evidence in the file"

CLAIM: Admission coverage is not decided by length of stay alone; the case facts give no patient clinical details.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Those cases that appear to be routine, expected discharge within 24 hours and which do not substantiate SI & IS criteria"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: Level of care needs individual determination; facts do not settle skilled need after the plateau.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "[p]lateau of benefits from skilled PT interventions reached at current mental level"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "the beneficiary must receive an individual level of care determination using existing administrative criteria and procedures"

CLAIM: Services duplicative of facility-required care are not reasonable and necessary, but facts do not show the nursing content.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "Services to people who already have access to appropriate care from a willing caregiver would not be considered reasonable and necessary"

CLAIM: Therapy was received but facts show discharge from PT/OT before the dates at issue and no skilled need for those dates.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She was discharged from OT on January 19, 2009, and from PT on January 22, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "For a discussion of skilled therapy (that is, PT, SLP, and OT) services in the context of the SNF level of care criteria"

CLAIM: Insulin dosage changes after nurse-forwarded logs show an unstabilized regimen needing skilled observation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.1): "skilled observation and treatment must be documented at each home health visit, until the patient's clinical condition and/or treatment regimen has stabilized"

CLAIM: SNF care was for hematuria treated in the qualifying hospital stay.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was diagnosed with hematuria secondary to prostate enlargement"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Timing of SNF admission after hospital stay is satisfied, but passages do not settle the need for continued therapy.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "Extended care services are “post-hospital” if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay"

CLAIM: Coverage needs an individualized assessment of skilled need; the facts are largely appellant assertions.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary demonstrated “slow but steady progress” reflecting gains in “safety, balance and overall functional mobility.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "skilled therapy services are covered when an individualized assessment of the patient’s clinical condition demonstrates"

CLAIM: Teaching safe stair/transfer technique can be reasonable, but facts are only appellant assertions.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely."

CLAIM: Complications require more frequent skilled care and are covered with documentation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He was hospitalized for several days in July 2007 for urosepsis and e.coli infection."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "where there are complications that require more frequent skilled care related to the catheter, such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered"

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care alone is not skilled, but this beneficiary had complications.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "A patient with a well-established colostomy absent complications may require assistance changing the colostomy bag"

CLAIM: Hour limits are stated, but no facts about skilled need are given.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Level of care needs an individual determination; facts do not show a skilled-need finding.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Physician’s Telephone Orders requiring intravenous and intramuscular medication for pain and morphine via a portacath"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "the beneficiary must receive an individual level of care determination using existing administrative criteria and procedures"

CLAIM: IRF necessity depends on individual care needs, which the facts do not describe.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "were Medicare coverage criteria met for the IRF services at issue"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "Medicare requires determinations of whether IRF stays are reasonable and necessary to be based on an assessment of each beneficiary's individual care needs"

CLAIM: Close nurse monitoring with medication changes shows potential to change treatment.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On August 5, 2009, the psychiatrist reduced her Haldol from three to two times a day"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "there is a reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient"

CLAIM: Pneumonia treatment with ongoing nursing monitoring is skilled observation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "and the beneficiary was diagnosed with pneumonia"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.3): "skilled nursing services are covered when an individualized assessment of the patient’s clinical condition demonstrates"

CLAIM: IRF care requires meeting all 42 CFR 412.622 requirements; facts do not show therapy intensity or preadmission screening.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Upon admission, the beneficiary’s functional status was as follows: moderate assistance supine to sit"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act if the patient meets all"

CLAIM: Record documents patient condition and functional deficits at PT start, as policy requires for skilled PT

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, J.M. required moderate to maximal assist with functional mobility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "Documentation of the patient’s condition in the medical record must describe the circumstances which delineate the need for skilled rather than"

CLAIM: Strength measurements (tests and measurements) are documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "J.M.’s right lower extremity strength measured 3/5 and left lower extremity measured 2+/5."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "tests and measurements of range of motion, strength, balance, coordination, endurance, and functional ability"

CLAIM: Nursing documentation describes skilled observation after fall

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses monitored J.M.’s condition including pupil size, alertness, signs and symptoms of pain and ability to follow commands."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "The medical documentation must describe the skilled services that require the involvement of nursing personnel"

CLAIM: Hospital records for a stay well over three days were submitted

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The provider submits, as evidence of the three-day stay, hospital records concerning the beneficiary’s December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Medical evidence in file shows ongoing medication adjustments

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "coverage would be determined based on a review of the medical evidence in the file"

CLAIM: Policy requires admission order/certification; case facts contain no admission order or certification evidence

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "is therefore required for all hospital inpatient cases for hospital inpatient coverage and payment under Part A"

CLAIM: Case facts discuss only liability and reopening, not the medical record content

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the appellant solely contests the ALJ’s findings concerning liability pursuant to Section 1879 of the Social Security Act (Act) and/or Section 1870 of the Act."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: Policy requires qualifying hospital stay record; case facts are procedural and show none

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant filed a timely request for Council review (Form DAB-101), dated August 24, 2009, and received on August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20): "must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least three consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: Notice of non-coverage is referenced as signed, but its content (written, reason, liability) is not in the case facts

CASE FACT QUOTED: "during the time the beneficiary signed the notice of non-coverage"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.3.1.1): "The beneficiary notice must meet the following criteria: a. It must be in writing."

CLAIM: A qualifying hospital stay is asserted but its length is not stated

CASE FACT QUOTED: "after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium, a urinary tract infection (UTI), and dehydration"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Policy requires supporting documentation for home health eligibility; case facts show no such records

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The ALJ decisions concerned nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.5.1.2): "must be able to provide, upon request, the supporting documentation that substantiates the eligibility for the Medicare home health benefit"

CLAIM: Residence is an assisted living facility; nothing shows whether it is primarily engaged in providing skilled services

CASE FACT QUOTED: "an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "An individual may be "confined to the home" for purposes of Medicare coverage of home health services if he or she resides in an institution"

CLAIM: Qualifying 3-day inpatient stay is required; the length of the GI bleeding stay is not documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: Skilled therapy records end before the billed dates; no skilled-care record is shown for January 28 onward

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She was discharged from OT on January 19, 2009, and from PT on January 22, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing need is documented in visit notes and records

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the records dated within this period include numerous documented instances of changes in the beneficiary’s medication schedule"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: Nurses documented assessment and physician contact on a possible urinary tract infection

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses contacted the beneficiary’s doctor to obtain permission to take a urine sample for analysis."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The nurse visits the patient and determines that the catheter is plugged and there are symptoms of a urinary tract infection."

CLAIM: Insulin dosage changes after nurse-reported blood sugar logs are recorded

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.13): "Where the documentation shows that the dosage is being adjusted, monitoring would be reasonable and necessary as ordered by the physician or allowed practitioner."

CLAIM: Hospital stay of more than 3 inpatient days (admission day counted, discharge day not) is documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010, for “worsening gross hematuria.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day."

CLAIM: Transfer to SNF occurred on the discharge date, within 30 days

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must also have been transferred to a participating SNF within 30 days after discharge from the hospital"

CLAIM: SNF care relates to the hematuria condition treated in the hospital, with physician-ordered skilled nursing documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "a physician indicated that the beneficiary required skilled nursing for one week to monitor for signs of fever, chills, clots"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Qualifying inpatient stay of at least three days is documented (August 16-25, 2011)

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011, for a “seizure-type episode.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: SNF admission on the discharge date meets the 30-day transfer window

CASE FACT QUOTED: "was first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "Extended care services are “post-hospital” if initiated within 30 days after discharge"

CLAIM: PT and OT services after readmission are recorded

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Following readmission, the beneficiary received physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and nursing services."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Policy requires an initial PT evaluation and active written treatment plan; case facts do not show either, only the appellant's assertions

CASE FACT QUOTED: "“new physical decline which warranted Physical Therapy . . . intervention in order to ensure continued safety and independence.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "an active written treatment plan that is based upon an initial evaluation performed by a qualified physical therapist"

CLAIM: Documentation of the need for skilled rather than unskilled services is required; facts only relay the appellant's claim about the documentation

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant asserts that the documentation of record, present throughout all levels of review, demonstrates the clear need for the skills of a physical therapist"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "Documentation of the patient’s condition in the medical record must describe the circumstances which delineate the need for skilled rather than"

CLAIM: Each component of maintenance program design must be documented in the home health record; facts give only appellant's assertions for W.B.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the therapist was “in the process of designing an appropriate home exercise program” for the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Each component of this process must be documented in the home health record."

CLAIM: Therapist must document why a maintenance program could not be developed; PT notes are cited for D.W. but their content is not given

CASE FACT QUOTED: "at 133 (PT notes of February 7, 2006), at 144 (PT notes of March 9, 2006), at 148 (PT notes of March 20, 2006)."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "the therapist must document why the maintenance program could not be developed during those last rehabilitative/restorative treatment visit(s)."

CLAIM: Skilled need is documented through nurse-noted complications of the ostomies

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses noted abscesses in the rectum."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: Complications requiring more frequent skilled care (fistula, tissue in urostomy) appear in the record

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "where there are complications that require more frequent skilled care related to the catheter, such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered"

CLAIM: Hospitalization and recurrent infections during the dates of service are recorded

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He was hospitalized for several days in July 2007 for urosepsis and e.coli infection."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "The medical condition of the patient must be described and documented to support the need for nursing skilled services"

CLAIM: Policy sets hour limits for part-time or intermittent care; case facts contain no records of hours or services furnished, only the appellant's argument

CASE FACT QUOTED: "whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services furnished to the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Qualifying criteria such as need for skilled care are not shown in the case facts

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the appellant argues that the ALJ failed to analyze whether the services furnished to each beneficiary were reasonable and necessary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40): "the patient must meet the qualifying criteria as specified in §30"

CLAIM: Direct admission to SNF following hospital discharge is documented

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was admitted to the appellant’s nursing facility, REMH, immediately following her discharge from the hospital"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "If the beneficiary is admitted to the SNF immediately following a 3-day qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified bed due to no certified bed available is recorded in the medical records

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s medical records indicate that she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant’s facility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "When patients who require SNF services are placed in a noncertified part of an institution which contains a participating “distinct part” SNF"

CLAIM: Physician-signed orders for skilled IV/IM medication document the SNF care need

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Physician’s Telephone Orders requiring intravenous and intramuscular medication for pain and morphine via a portacath are also included for the second admission."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: IRF coverage depends on an individual assessment of care needs; case facts are procedural and contain no clinical records

CASE FACT QUOTED: "were Medicare coverage criteria met for the IRF services at issue[?]"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "Medicare requires determinations of whether IRF stays are reasonable and necessary to be based on an assessment of each beneficiary's individual care needs."

CLAIM: Only a physician testimony and claim dates are mentioned, not the IRF documentation

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Dr. K.F., appellant’s Medical Director, testified."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: Psychiatric observation needs are carefully documented through nurse, physician and APRN monitoring

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day), one or more physicians, and the psychiatric APRN"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Therefore, these cases must be carefully documented."

CLAIM: Nurses' findings led to treatment changes (pneumonia diagnosis, antibiotic), documented in the record

CASE FACT QUOTED: "They notified the medical director, a chest x-ray was taken, and the beneficiary was diagnosed with pneumonia."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "there is a reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient"

CLAIM: Hospital admission preceded SNF admission within the 30-day window

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On July 27, 2009, the beneficiary was admitted to Twin Maples Health Care Facility, the appellant’s SNF."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must also have been transferred to a participating SNF within 30 days after discharge from the hospital"

CLAIM: Daily skilled PT is documented from admission

CASE FACT QUOTED: "physical therapy (PT) was started five times a week"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.4): "There must be specific evidence that daily skilled nursing or skilled rehabilitation services are required and received"

CLAIM: Policy requires a preadmission screening within 48 hours of IRF admission; the case facts do not mention one
